resources.name: LFP Router Fingerprinting Artifacts
quotes: Lightweight FingerPrinting (LFP), a novel lightweight, accurate, and more complete remote vendor fingerprinting methodology and tool (§3).
LFP is publicly available, along with the the derived signatures and classification results from this study to enable reproducibility and future work [3].
references: [3] Taha Albakour, Oliver Gasser, Robert Beverly, and Georgios Smaragdakis. 2023. Illuminating Router Vendor Diversity Within Providers and Along Network Paths (artifacts). https://routerfingerprinting.github.io/.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The paper introduces LFP as its primary methodology and tool for router vendor fingerprinting.

resources.name: ITDK
quotes: we leverage two complementary public router datasets: the RIPE Atlas traceroutes dataset [43] and the ITDK dataset [11].
In addition to IP level traceroute data, we also use the router topology from CAIDA’s February 2022 ITDK [11].
references: [11] CAIDA. 2021. Macroscopic Internet Topology Data Kit (ITDK). https://www.caida.org/catalog/datasets/internet-topology-data-kit/.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The authors use the ITDK dataset to select target router IPs and perform router-level analysis.

resources.name: Censys Universal Internet Dataset
quotes: For this, we acquire a set of addresses from Censys, which are known to reveal vendor information through service banners.
references: [17] Zakir Durumeric, David Adrian, Ariana Mirian, Michael Bailey, and J. Alex Halderman. 2015. A Search Engine Backed by Internet-Wide Scanning. In ACM CCS.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: Censys data is used to acquire a set of addresses for evaluating the accuracy of LFP against known vendor information.

resources.name: CAIDA|AS Relationships
quotes: Next, we use the CAIDA AS relationship dataset [12] to find AS paths where these vendor homogeneous ASes serve as transit ASes.
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: The CAIDA AS relationship dataset is used to identify AS paths for the informed routing case study.

resources.name: MIDAR
quotes: alias resolution tools such as MIDAR [29] and Ally [47] use monotonic IPID counters to infer aliases
This complementary dataset contains router alias sets (excluding singletons) inferred via MIDAR [29] and iffinder measurements.
references: [29] K. Keys, Y. Hyun, M. Luckie, and k claffy. 2013. Internet-Scale IPv4 Alias Resolution with MIDAR. IEEE/ACM Trans. Networking 21, 2 (2013).
resources.used_in_paper_reasoning: MIDAR is mentioned as an example of an alias resolution tool and as a tool used to create the ITDK dataset, but is not actively used by the authors for their own measurements.
